headline: LG Electronics India promoter to sell up to 2% stake to meet SEBI public shareholding norms
hook: LG reduces promoter stake, public float rises

modes.bear: Promoter stake cut signals possible governance concerns, triggering a 3% intraday sell‑off.
modes.bull: Divestment raises public float, enhancing liquidity and potentially supporting a higher valuation.
modes.simple: LG Electronics India’s promoter will sell up to 2% of its shares to meet SEBI rules, increasing the public shareholding and may affect the stock’s price and liquidity.

summary: LG Electronics Inc. announced it will sell up to 2% of its holding in LG Electronics India via open‑market transactions to comply with SEBI's minimum public shareholding requirements. The sale of about 13.6 million shares can be done in tranches and must be completed by Dec 31 2026, lowering the promoter's stake from 85% to roughly 83%. The news pushed the stock down as much as 3% intraday, though it closed 2.3% higher the next day. The increased public float may improve liquidity and affect valuation, which matters to Indian retail investors holding the stock.
why_it_matters: Higher public float may improve stock liquidity
winners_losers: Minority shareholders gain / promoter stake reduced
